newsitem.title: USA: EU's Fischler mum on 1998 cereals setaside.
newsitem.headline: EU's Fischler mum on 1998 cereals setaside.

text.p: Franz Fischler, agriculture commissioner for the European Union, refused Monday to discuss possible cropland setasides for next year's cereals crops.
Fischler, in response to a question from Reuters, said a clear picture of the size of this year's harvest was needed before the setaside could be fixed. A proposal will be presented in July, he said.

France has advocated a zero percent setaside, down from this year's five percent. In May, diplomats said the five percent setaside might be repeated as a compromise between France and Germany, which favors a larger setaside.
"We have no stocks," Fischler said, referring to the 1.83 million tonnes of intervention stocks on hand at June 12, compared to 2.6 million tonnes last July 1.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman was expected at a meeting later in the day to criticize the export taxes used by the EU as a way to ensure adequate domestic supplies.

Fischler brushed aside a question about the U.S. goal in the next round of world trade talks for elimination or reduction of the power of state trading enterprises (STEs). He said it was a question for Canada, Australia and New Zealand, the nations commonly criticized for marketing boards that hold monopoly power over some ag exports.
For more than a year, the United States has tried to enlist allies against STEs.
